$comment: THE reproducibility configuration. Every decision that could change a reported
number is recorded here rather than living in a script's default argument, so
that 'we used alpha = 0.05' is checkable rather than assertable. `verify.js`
reads this file and fails the build when the artifact and this record disagree.
Two things are deliberately NOT here. Model weights are not ours to pin, so the
judge identifiers are recorded with the date they were reached and the paper
says that a re-run against a silently updated endpoint is a different
experiment. And the human annotation labels do not exist yet: the study is
PENDING, and the config records its design so that the absence is legible.

frozenBecause: It is the record the previously reported results rest on.
Two of its four generator arms (llama-3.3-70b-versatile, and the
llama-3.1-8b-instant used by the multi-candidate experiment) are no longer
reachable on this key, so regenerating would silently produce a different
Growth is APPENDED under its own seed and manifest; the original 955 remain byte-identical.

splits.method: 50/50 stratified by (category, generator), fixed seed; attack categories held out of calibration entirely

growth.reason: Task 4 - S3 (the motivating example) and D3 carried named qualitative claims at n=8 and n=5 test pairs
growth.note: Additive only. Every original id, pair content, split and score is unchanged, which is why the frozen annotation sheet still verifies against the grown corpus.

v2ext.note: Strictly additive to v1. Never merged into corpus/pairs.jsonl; analyses report v1, the extension, and their union separately.
v2ext.splitMethod: deterministic alternation within each (category, tool, generator) stratum; attack categories are split='attack' and never enter calibration

ladder.note: One act family declared three ways. Every pair exists at every level, so level comparisons are paired item-by-item.

judges.scoreContract: integer 0-100 only; 0.95 is REJECTED rather than rescaled; out-of-range values are rejected rather than clamped; a pair that never receives an admissible value is recorded as null (abstention) and never imputed

llama-3.3-70b-versatile.role: v1 only — endpoint no longer available on this key

llama-3.1-8b-instant.role: v1 multi-candidate experiment only — endpoint no longer available on this key

admission.rationale: Coverage alone is insufficient. A judge that answers every pair with the same number has 100% coverage, produces a threshold equal to that constant, suppresses nothing under the strict inequality, and therefore reports 0% wrong-suppression and 0% deduplication — the same fake-perfect row an abstaining judge produces. Both routes are closed.

calibration.thresholdConstruction: t_hi(m) = ceil((n+1)(1 - alpha/m))-th smallest calibration score; +Infinity when that index exceeds n
calibration.multiplicity: Bonferroni over the candidate set (union bound, valid under arbitrary dependence). Direct set-conformal calibration is implemented for comparison.
calibration.escalationFloor: t_lo = floor((n+1)*gamma)-th smallest SAME-pair score, capped at t_hi
calibration.poolRule: MUST be drawn from the configuration's own jurisdiction — the pairs its layers actually route to the judge. Enforced in src/evaluate.js:jurisdictionFilter.
calibration.abstentions: dropped from the pool; excluded from the max; can never suppress

policies.num: numeric normal form; thousands separators stripped; trailing zeros dropped
policies.text: NFC + trim + internal whitespace collapse; deliberately NOT semantic

witnessProjections.declared: canonical values of all non-text fields
witnessProjections.tightened: the above plus the numeric magnitudes each free-text field mentions

statistics.intervalRationale: Wald collapses to zero width at p=0 and p=1, which is exactly where the headline rates sit
statistics.pairedTest: exact two-sided McNemar over discordant items
statistics.multipleComparisons: Holm-Bonferroni, applied WITHIN a family (liveness and safety corrected separately)
statistics.zeroReporting: rates that are zero by construction are marked and distinguished from zeros that are sample estimates

crashReplay.crossFamilyRationale: a judge scoring paraphrases written by its own family is partly measuring self-recognition
crashReplay.providerIdempotency: ABSENT BY DESIGN — the mock provider presents no idempotency key, so the commit window stays open and measurable rather than being closed by an assumption

labelValidation.$comment: Two channels. H is human annotators and was NEVER COLLECTED. M is a panel of language models and ran. They are never pooled and never described interchangeably.
labelValidation.preregistration: annotation/PREREGISTRATION.md (written and committed before any judgement was collected)
labelValidation.freeze: annotation/FREEZE.json — 154 items, sheet hash 66a174e1392093c14e911d6130b235b3d4af3b8116c0a81ef27830174a249a9c, export seed 20260818; re-checked by annotationFreezeCheck
labelValidation.adjudication: majority of 3; ties and UNSURE-dominated items go to a fourth independent adjudicator, never to a coin flip
labelValidation.blinding: annotators see the two calls only; no labels, predictions, thresholds, attack flags; presentation order and A/B assignment randomised per annotator by the instrument

channelM.whatItIs: a blinded panel of language models — NOT a human study, and never to be reported as one
channelM.panel: groq/compound, groq/compound-mini, qwen/qwen3.6-27b; adjudicator openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b; openai/gpt-oss-120b barred as the judge whose scores the re-derivation uses
channelM.responsesAnalysed: annotation/preregistered-collection (earliest committed state, 117 fully annotated items)
disclosedDefects: 93 of the 154 sheet items come from an extension corpus whose judge scores were never persisted; in the preregistered 'as executed' re-derivation they abstain, escalate, and so enter the wrong-suppression denominator without being able to enter its numerator. 12 of the 14 label flips are such items. Both 'as executed' and 'scored only' forms are reported.
The published figures are not exactly reproducible from any committed state of the response files: the analysis ran against live files. See annotation/RESPONSE-PROVENANCE.md.

channelH.whatRemains: recruit 3 independent annotators and 1 adjudicator; collect responses-<name>.csv into a directory of its own; commit it; then run annotation.js --ingest --responses-dir <dir> --channel H
channelH.mustNotBeClaimed: No manuscript may describe the existing evidence as human validation; verify.js fails the build if one does.

cost.source: results/aij_analyses.json -> A8_cost, computed by aijAnalyses.js from the judge session metadata in results/judge_meta-*.json
cost.denominator: tokens of a scoring session divided by the pairs scored IN THAT SESSION
cost.priorDefect: an earlier cost model divided one session's tokens by every pair ever scored, understating cost by roughly an order of magnitude (5,431 tokens per 1,000 dispatches reported; ~140,000 measured for the primary judge). Corrected 2026-09.
cost.batching: judges are called in batches of 10 pairs, so the system prompt is amortised over the batch; per-comparison figures inherit that batching and would be higher at batch size 1
cost.callsPer1000Dispatches: follows from the judge's jurisdiction: 762 calls per 1,000 dispatches under the declared schema (76.2% residual), 589 under the refined one (58.9%)

list: calibration and test splits share no pair id
attack pairs never appear in the calibration split
every stored score is null or an exact integer percent in [0,1]
no score was clamped into range
abstentions are stored as null and are absent from every calibration pool
no abstention results in a SUPPRESS decision
every judge reported with rates satisfies the admission rule
candidate-set multiplicity never exceeds the certified capacity without the threshold becoming +Infinity
every configuration's calibration pool is drawn from its own jurisdiction
labels are exactly SAME or DIFF
the human-annotation result file does not claim COMPLETE while no responses exist

classConditional.$comment: AIJ revision Phase 2. Offline; persisted scores only. Mondrian over DIFF categories is an oracle analysis (category is label-defined); the deployable class-valid rule is the maximum per-category threshold. Reweighting shifts the RESIDUAL distinct test mix toward D3, remaining weight split D1:D2 in observed ratio.

$comment: AIJ revision Phase 3. PREPARED, NOT RUN. Units are built from corpus v1: one per residual TEST pair; dispatch = pair.b, candidate 1 = pair.a (true match for SAME units, labelled distinct act for DIFF units); candidates 2..mMax drawn without replacement by a seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle from corpus inputs of the same tool that share the dispatch projection, are outside its SAME-class, and are known distinct (different seed act, or linked by a DIFF label). Thresholds from the deployed configuration jurisdiction-matched pool; uncorrected t(alpha) vs Bonferroni t(alpha/m).

channelHTargeted.scope: targeted follow-up on the two strata contested by the model panel; NOT the preregistered 154-item study
channelHTargeted.materialsSource: annotation/preregistered-collection/ (INSTRUCTIONS.md hash-checked against FREEZE.json; instrument.html with its item list reduced to the packet)
channelHTargeted.contestedRule: Wilson 95% upper bound of agreement < 0.80; with 15 items per stratum, contested at <= 8 agreeing

scoringStability.$comment: TMLR revision. Every residual pair of corpus v1 (cal+test) re-scored once by the primary judge in batches of ten from one seeded shuffle, so pool and test share a scoring context; compared with the persisted scoring (and the multi-candidate run as a third scoring of the test pairs).
